title: App classes come from local CSS Modules
intent: Paint follows the theme, and a framework control keeps the styling and focus treatment it ships with, so every palette holds its contrast and a control looks and behaves the same in every app. Inline style and a hardcoded colour in app script paint around the palette, and a class on a framework control restyles what the framework owns. So a class reaches only a native element, through a direct property naming a class its sibling CSS Module defines; a framework control is configured through its props. Inline style, any other class name and colour literals in app script are refused.
reference: Layout via Stack, Grid, DetailList and the page archetypes from @terpjs/react-core. A layout a component owns: import styles from "./Board.module.css" and className={styles.board} on a native element, in the body of a plain Page. Paint via the design tokens, var(--color-...).

runtime.rationale: Most of the rule is erased before the app serves: react-core sets inline styles of its own, and a CSS Module's class is a hashed name like any other in the built DOM, so neither a style nor a class on a native element can be attributed to app authorship there. One part can be. Every react-core control's root carries a data-terp marker and react-core renders no class on it, save the router's active link, so a class on a framework control is observable in the running page, on the seam the archetype slot check (verifySlotChildren) already walks by those markers. A refusal there has not shipped.
runtime.tracking: docs/decisions/0217-app-components-can-own-a-scoped-stylesheet.md in the reference implementation, the Consequences section: a runtime refusal of a class on a data-terp element, beside verifySlotChildren, flips this entry to required.
